newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - July 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Football League Players' Association yesterday said its members would rather be suspended than fined for minor offences. The AFLPA's preference is for the fines system where a player loses 1/52 of his base rate and one match payment, but plyers prefer a one match suspension because they only have to forfeit 50 per cent of their fee to the club. Page 22.

Olympic silver medallist swimmer Scott Miller has withdrawn from next month's Pan Pacific championships in Japan, due to an ongoing shoulder injury which has hampered his training. Miller was concerned that contesting the Pan Pacifics would leave him unprpared for the World Championships trials in October. Page 21.

Leading Brisbane sports lawyer Dennis Boucher yesterday said jockeys would face increasing claims for damages where their negligence caused race-track incidents resulting in the injury or death of racehorses. There are currently two such cases before cours in South Australia. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Super League chief Ian Frykberg said yesterday a Melbourne rugby league team would have to prove itself capable of being self-supporting before it was included in any national competition. Melbourne franchise holder John Ribot said he was more concerned wth peace negotiations between Super League and the Australian Rugby League at the moment. Page 53.

Veteran Australian striker Graham Arnold, who now plays club soccer in Japan, wants the Australian Socceroos to face Japan in the final qualifying match for next year's World Cup finals. While Japan is the highest ranked Asian team, they have only beaten ustralia twice from eleven matches since 1956, and reportedly fear facing the Socceroos. Page 53.

Australian rugby union coach Greg Smith has intensified pressure on Bledisloe Cup referee Ed Morrison to properly police the New Zealand All Blacks when the two teams clash at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Saturday night. Smith was unimpressed with Morrison's refereeing of the first match in Christchurch. Page 54.
THE AGE

Television coverage of Australian Football League matches may be revolutionised with games split between the major networks. Kerry Packer, a joint bidder for the Docklands project, has demanded television rights be included in the deal, and is heavily favured to win coverage rights after Seven's agreement expires after 2001. It is likely his Nine Network, already committed to extensive sports coverage would then sell the rights to some of the games. Page B8.

Apprentice jockey Brent Stanley has decided not to ride at Cheltenham on Saturday, which, with only two city meetings until the end of the season, makes it virtually impossible for him to overtake Brett Prebble to be this season's leading apprentice. Preble who leads Stanley by four winners is set to win his third consecutive apprentices' premiership. Page B6.

Auzsports promoter Tony Francis said yesterday the Greek basketball federation was to blame for the 37-point defeat of the touring Greek All-Stars against a second-string Melbourne Magic side earlier this week. Francis said the Greek federation had decide to send younger players instead of the original plan for the best Greek players. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Western Bulldogs defender Matthew Dent last night became the sixth player from the team to be suspended this season and the ninth to face the Australian Football League Tribunal. Football manager Garry O'Sullivan said last night a tough and uncompromisingbrand of football was the reason so many Bulldogs players had faced the tribunal this season. Page 88.

St Kilda's Nicky Winmar has admitted he almost quit football last month due to poor form and the pressure of expectations. Only five weeks after being dropped from the senior team for missing training, Winmar will become the first Aboriginal player to comete in 200 Australian Football League games when his team meets Brisbane on Sunday. Page 88.

Australian high-jumper Tim Forsyth produced his best jump of the European season at a small meet in Budapest overnight. Forsyth jumped 2.32 metres to win the event, and is working back to the form that saw him jump 2.36 metres at the Australian championshps in March, the world's best performance this year. Page 80.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

An International Amateur Boxing Association decision to put a ceiling on the number of competitors in each weight category at the Sydney 2000 Olympics will make it tougher for Australian competitors to be included because, unlike other sports where the hot country gains automatic selection, in boxing Australia is included in the Oceania category. Page 90.

The Australian Rugby League has proposed to strip Queensland of its hosting of the major qualifying final, scheduled for Suncorp Stadium in September, for fear it will be a financial disaster, after poor attendances for Queensland Crushers and State of Orgin games this year. Page 86.

Super League referees coordinator Ian Smith says the New Zealand Referees Association was wasting its time in seeking exclusive rights for Kiwi referees to control Super League matches played in New Zealand. Page 94.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
